title: Idempotent Tool Execution
summary: Make repeated attempts at one business operation converge on one recorded effect, even when agents, queues, or networks deliver the request more than once.
overview: Idempotent execution lets a caller safely repeat an operation without repeating its intended business effect. Agent systems need this because model loops, worker recovery, queue redelivery, and network timeouts can all create duplicate attempts. The idempotency identity belongs to the business operation, not to an individual HTTP attempt.

Persist the key with a canonical request fingerprint and the operation result. A repeated key with different parameters must be rejected rather than silently treated as the original request. Exactly-once delivery is generally not the useful promise; design for repeated delivery with controlled effects and explicit reconciliation of uncertain outcomes.

production.poc: A prototype can assign one stable key to each simulated command and test duplicate submission. Do not generate a fresh key inside retry logic.
production.production: Production atomically claims operation identity, stores status and results, and coordinates with the actual side effect. If the remote system cannot participate, use its idempotency support or a reconciliation protocol.
production.scale: At scale, choose key scope and retention from the maximum replay horizon. Expiring keys too early allows delayed duplicates, while retaining them indefinitely increases storage and data-management cost.

components.name: Operation identity
components.role: Names the intended business action across retries, workers, and model turns.

components.name: Request fingerprint
components.role: Canonicalizes meaningful parameters and detects conflicting reuse of a key.

components.name: Idempotency ledger
components.role: Atomically tracks pending, completed, failed, and uncertain operation outcomes.

components.name: Tool adapter
components.role: Passes stable identity to supported downstream APIs and normalizes responses.

components.name: Reconciler
components.role: Resolves ambiguous outcomes using authoritative business records before another attempt.

flow.title: Define operation
flow.description: Derive or create a stable key for the specific business intent and tenant scope.

flow.title: Validate fingerprint
flow.description: Compare canonical parameters with any existing entry for that key.

flow.title: Claim execution
flow.description: Atomically reserve the operation or return the already recorded result.

flow.title: Perform effect
flow.description: Invoke the downstream command with matching idempotency support where available.

flow.title: Commit result
flow.description: Store the authoritative outcome and response reference before acknowledging completion.

flow.title: Reconcile uncertainty
flow.description: If confirmation is lost, query operation status and reuse the same key for any permitted retry.

diagrams.title: Repeated delivery with one business effect
diagrams.code:
sequenceDiagram
 participant A as Agent worker
 participant L as Idempotency ledger
 participant T as Order service
 A->>L: Claim operation key and request hash
 L-->>A: New operation accepted
 A->>T: Create replacement with stable key
 T-->>A: Replacement identifier
 A->>L: Store completed result
 A->>L: Retry same key after lost response
 L-->>A: Return existing replacement result
diagrams.caption: Duplicate attempts resolve to the recorded operation, while conflicting parameters are rejected.

diagrams.title: Conflicting reuse and uncertain outcomes
diagrams.code:
stateDiagram-v2
 [*] --> Unseen
 Unseen --> Pending: Atomically claim key and fingerprint
 Pending --> Completed: Authoritative effect confirmed
 Pending --> Uncertain: Response lost
 Uncertain --> Completed: Reconciliation finds effect
 Uncertain --> Pending: Safe retry with same key
 Completed --> Completed: Same key and same intent
 Pending --> Conflict: Same key with changed parameters
 Completed --> Conflict: Same key with changed parameters
 Conflict --> [*]
diagrams.caption: A key identifies one intent. Changed parameters are a conflict, while uncertain outcomes require reconciliation.

useCase.title: Avoiding duplicate replacement shipments
useCase.situation: A retailer's assistant creates replacement shipments after staff approve damaged-product cases.
useCase.problem: The shipping API can accept a request and then lose the response, causing the agent to issue a second shipment.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must recover from uncertainty without sending duplicate goods.
useCase.architecture: A replacement operation key binds the claim, order line, approved quantity, and tenant to an idempotency ledger and downstream request.
runtime: The worker claims the key, submits the replacement, and stores the shipping system's identifier.
A retry from another worker returns the existing result or reconciles the pending operation before attempting delivery again.
useCase.failure: If the same key arrives with a changed address or quantity, the gateway rejects the conflict and requires a new explicitly authorized business operation.
useCase.impact: Measure duplicate effects, unresolved operations, conflicting-key reuse, and reconciliation latency. The ledger alone cannot guarantee safety if the external command bypasses its protocol.

tradeoffs.benefit: Retries become safer across worker and network failure.
tradeoffs.cost: Every command requires storage and identity discipline.
Ledger size and retention obligations increase.

tradeoffs.benefit: The effect boundary can enforce duplicate prevention directly.
tradeoffs.cost: Provider semantics and key scope must be understood.

failures.scenario: Worker crashes after effect but before ledger update
failures.detection: Operation remains pending while the business record exists.
failures.recovery: Query the downstream key or business identity and record the confirmed result.

failures.detection: Replay arrives outside the deduplication window.
failures.recovery: Align retention with replay horizons and add business-level uniqueness where possible.

mistakes.mistake: Generating a new key for every attempt
mistakes.fix: Create the key once per business intent.
Persist identity across restarts and workers.

mistakes.mistake: Treating identical text as identical intent
mistakes.fix: Use explicit operation identity and canonical parameters.

whenToUse: Tools create or modify business records.
Retries, replay, or duplicate delivery are possible.
External effects can expose stable identity or reconciliation.
whenNotToUse: The operation is a pure read with no side effects.
A repeated action is intentionally a new business request.
The downstream effect cannot be identified or reconciled safely.
checklist: Define key scope and replay lifetime.
Preserve keys across every retry layer.
